subject: Materials Science
title: Yield Strength: The Point of No Return
description: Learn Yield Strength: The Point of No Return in one minute.

hook.text: Bend a paperclip gently and it springs back. Bend it too far and it stays bent forever.

buildup.text: Yield strength is the stress at which permanent deformation begins — the elastic limit.

discovery.text: Below yield, atoms stretch but return to position. Above yield, dislocations move and shape changes permanently.

twist.text: The 0.2% offset method defines yield for metals without a sharp transition — a practical engineering convention.

climax.text: Structural steel is designed so working stress never exceeds yield — usually with a safety factor of 1.5 to 2.

punchline.text: Stay below yield and the material remembers its shape. Cross it and it doesn't.

quiz.question: What happens when stress exceeds yield strength?
